title: H-Index
statement: A researcher has h-index h when h of their papers have at least h citations each, and the other papers have at most h citations each. `citations[i]` is the citation count of paper i. Return the researcher's h-index.
hints: Sort descending. The h-index is the largest h such that the h-th paper has at least h citations.
If citations is sorted descending, paper i (1-based) supports h = i when citations[i - 1] >= i.
A counting bucket of size n + 1 also computes it in linear time, because any count above n is equivalent to n.

approaches.name: Counting sort
approaches.explanation: Bucket citation counts clipped at n.

editorial: After sorting descending, walk i from 1. While the i-th paper has at least i citations, h can be i. Stop at the first paper that does not. That h is maximal because a larger value would require the next paper to have even more citations.
